newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Lebanon minister says Israel has no peace policy.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon minister says Israel has no peace policy.

text.p: Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Tuesday Israel's new government had no peace policy and was trying to "put world public opinion to sleep" to wipe out previous agreements.

"Since the new Israeli government has been in power, it has completely backed off the peace process, even if a few misleading points are made here and there," he said in a speech to the General Assembly.

Alluding to the Likud government headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected last May, he said: "Quite simply, there is an attempt to put world public opinion to sleep in order to wipe out what was agreed to at the (Madrid 1991) peace conference and the negotiations that followed."
Bouez said it was "clear that Israel has no peace policy. It has a policy which seeks to change the situation, to go back to threat, defiance, to the policies of expansion and colonisation."

Referring to a Middle East summit in Washington on Tuesday aimed at restarting negotiations between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, he said Israel would benefit from the U.S. electoral climate by removing all substance from steps taken.
President Bill Clinton called the summit after violence in Jerusalem, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip last week that took the lives of 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
